correctness.rationale: For any beta>0, the angular clock gives E exp(i(Theta_t-Theta_s))=exp[-kappa|t^beta-s^beta|]. The exact time-integrated velocity covariance gives the inherited MSD. The integration-by-parts identity turns position into a weighted Brownian martingale and a remainder of order 1+T^(1-beta)_+; its infinite tail has a remainder bounded by 2v T^(1-beta)/(kappa beta). The angular second-harmonic covariance exp[-4kappa|u-w|] and Young convolution inequality give vanishing normalized quadratic-covariation anisotropy; martingale CLTs supply all three precisely normalized Gaussian laws. The martingale has finite terminal L2 norm exactly when beta>2, giving a.s. localization. A nondegenerate Gaussian scaling precludes a finite endpoint in probability below the threshold. Tonelli/Beta integration establishes the exact finite terminal second moment. The packaged verify.py passed 64 finite checks.

value.rationale: The complete law separates three qualitatively different regimes of a constant-speed, unconfined active particle: polynomial Gaussian spreading, critical logarithmic Gaussian spreading, and a.s. localization with an isotropic Gaussian endpoint-error law. The phase boundary beta=2 is forced by integrability of the martingale variance, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The theorem answers a natural mathematical-physics transport question left beyond the beta<2 numerical regime of the motivating study, and its distributional content is not a routine consequence of previously known second moments.
